description.p: vid-fp finds copies of the same video, even when they are not the same file. It fingerprints each video from its keyframes, so it still finds a match after a video has been re-encoded at another resolution, bitrate, frame rate, codec or container, and when one file is only a section of another.

ul.li: The same video re-encoded at a different resolution, bitrate or quality
The same video in a different container: MP4, MKV, AVI, MOV, WebM, TS and more
A clip, highlight or excerpt cut out of a longer recording
Copies under different names, in different folders, across several drives

description.p: Pick folders and start the scan, then go through the groups and choose which videos to move to the Trash. For each video the scan suggests whether to keep or delete it, and nothing is marked until you ask. The frames behind a match can be compared side by side, with a chart of where one video sits in the other.
The command-line tool is included as well: flatpak run --command=vid-fp io.github.danielnara24.vid-fp --help

The frames a clip shares with the film it was cut from, on one time scale
Folders and options, after a scan

description.p: One progress bar for the whole scan, which moves steadily from start to finish, including while videos are being compared.
The Flatpak is available again. Nothing else changed from 0.41.0.

Many more kinds of copies are found: mirrored videos, vertical and zoomed re-uploads, a video shown inside another, 4:3 and letterboxed broadcasts with captions in the bars, and clips whose frames fall between the source's keyframes. Each frame is compared on a second, finer hash, which keeps unrelated look-alikes apart. Videos sampled at every frame no longer match unrelated footage by chance, and comparing is faster. Every video is fingerprinted again once after the update.

Byte-identical copies are recognised and marked as identical copies, and are decoded only once. A video that was moved, renamed or touched keeps its fingerprint instead of being decoded again. The command line can check new files against an existing library with --against.

A Compare window shows the frames behind each match. HEVC videos are timed correctly when built against FFmpeg 6, so every video's fingerprint is made again once after the update. A Trash or recycle bin inside a scanned folder is no longer scanned.
